messages:
maria_support: Heads-up — getting a surge of auth/502 errors for org_999 after the config push at ~12:10 UTC. Customers in eu-west-1 seeing huge latency spikes, then clients fall back to us-east-1 and everything times out. Repro steps + snippets below, can someone triage? cc @kevin_eng @ingrid_oncall :eyes:

kevin_eng: on it. can you paste one raw request/response pair and a request-id?

maria_support: yes — sample header + response we captured:
Request-ID: req_0a1b2c3d
POST /v1/generate  Host: api.redwood.ai
Authorization: Bearer <redacted>
Response: 502 Bad Gateway
{"error":"upstream_http_502","trace":"trace-abc123"}

ingrid_oncall: quick hypothesis: sounds like SDK retry/backoff + hedged requests are causing cross-region failover loops when auth fails transiently. If the SDK hedges to multiple regions and the auth check fails in one region, the fallback logic might retry against another region with stale token causing auth errors everywhere.

maria_support: here's the client SDK config we saw in the app: ```js
{
  regionFallback: ["eu-west-1","us-east-1"],
  hedgedRequests: true,
  maxRetries: 5,
  backoffMs: 200
}
```

support-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-451 (auto) — linked to org_999. Pinging eng-runtime.

eng-runtime: looking. if hedgedRequests opens parallel connections to multiple regions, the first auth failure can cause the routing table to mark eu-West as unhealthy and clients to flip to us-east, then back, producing a "retry storm". we need to confirm whether the router honors token scope per-region.

devops_sam: I can pull router logs for req_0a1b2c3d — getting them now. quick ask: did the org recently rotate keys or enable IP-restrictions?

maria_support: no key rotation reported. customer says they did enable new enforcement rule (restrict token to eu-west-1) earlier today.

ingrid_oncall: that explains it — token is scoped to eu-west-1, but client hedged to us-east-1, so auth fails on us-east and router fallback kicks in repeatedly. Two action items: 1) advise customer to disable hedgedRequests or add regionAffinity while we patch routing logic; 2) eng-runtime to add guard so region-scoped tokens are not hedged to non-scoped regions.

kevin_eng: temporary mitigation we can tell them: set hedgedRequests=false and set regionFallback: ["eu-west-1"] OR enable regionAffinity:true. Example CLI change: ```yaml
client:
  hedgedRequests: false
  regionAffinity: true
  regionFallback: ["eu-west-1"]
```

maria_support: i'll send that to the customer as an immediate workaround. also asking them to provide full headers for a failing request so devops_sam can match logs.

devops_sam: pasted router trace for req_0a1b2c3d: "route: eu-west-1 -> auth failed 401 -> fallback to us-east-1 -> auth failed 401 -> mark eu-west degraded -> client retried -> repeated". Uploading full trace to INC-2026-451.

eng-runtime: assigned to eng-runtime@redwood. We should also add a short-term server-side fix: if token is region-scoped (claims include 'region'), do not route hedged requests to other regions and return a single definitive auth error instead of triggering fallback. I'll open a PR for a soft-fail change.

maria_support: great. ETA to customer for workaround note? I'll message them now and keep ticket updated.

ingrid_oncall: follow-up: post-mortem skeleton in INC-2026-451. Marking as P2 for now since it's customer-impacting. :white_check_mark:

kevin_eng: thanks everyone. actionables: support -> customer workaround; devops -> full trace; eng-runtime -> guard + PR. Keep me looped for deploy windows.

maria_support: noted. I'll update last_message_ts once the customer confirms the workaround.
